title: Deduplicate ingress counts on proxy key rebinds
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: We are observing duplicated ingress usage records for a subset of customers when workspace-level proxy keys are rotated or rebound across subprojects. Symptoms: duplicated per-token/ingress counts, transient spikes in per-workspace token usage and quota exhaustion, and downstream billing events with nearly-identical timestamps. This appears to affect only proxy-key style integrations (subproject proxies) and only when control plane rebinds happen under load. Goal: make attribution idempotent across rebinds and eliminate transient double-charges without regressing latency or dropping legitimate usage.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a workspace with 3 subprojects and a shared proxy key configured for ingress routing.
2) Start a sustained traffic generator (~200 rps) against the proxy key targeting different subprojects.
3) Trigger a key rebind via control-plane API: POST /v1/keys/:id/rebind which creates a new proxy handler and retires the old one.
4) Observe billing ingestion and usage-aggregator logs for the workspace during the 0-10s window after rebind.
5) Result: duplicated ingress entries appear in the usage_ledger table and Grafana shows a spike in token usage and billing events with matching request IDs but different attribution rows.
investigation_notes: Logs show the same inbound request ID hitting both the old handler and the new handler in a ~2-4s overlap during rebind. The control-plane issues a rebind, updates routing metadata, and meanwhile both handlers write attribution records to the usage-collector without a shared idempotency key. The usage-collector currently dedupes by (request_id, tenant_id) but the proxy rebind path rewrites tenant_id for the new handler to the subproject alias, causing the dedupe filter to miss duplicates. Additionally, a Kafka consumer rebalance can cause the same event to be processed twice if the producer emitted the same aggregated event from both handlers. DB traces show two insert attempts within 150ms with different attribution keys. Tracing: span correlation shows the ingress trace is forked at the proxy-auth layer; correlation headers preserved (x-rw-request-id) but the usage pipeline reads x-rw-tenant-alias which differs between handlers.
root_cause: Race between concurrent handlers during proxy-key rebind where attribution writes lack a global idempotency key. Rebind changes tenant aliasing semantics so dedupe logic that depends on tenant_id fails. Combined with streaming consumer rebalances, duplicate events are materialized in the billing ledger.
impact_summary: Affected customers see transient doubled usage counts and sometimes quota hits. Billing reconciliations show duplicate line-items for affected windows. Frequency: reported by 6 customers over the last 2 weeks; estimated 0.05% of total requests during key rotation windows. Severity: medium (unexpected billing noise and quota surprises).
reproducible: intermittent - reliably reproducible in test when rebinds run under sustained traffic
short_term_mitigation: 1) Add a temporary server-side gate in the collector: if two attribution writes arrive with identical x-rw-request-id within 10s, ignore the later write (apply on a short canonical window).
2) Ask infra to throttle rebind frequency for affected customers until fix is deployed.
3) Notify affected customers and create billing adjustments for confirmed duplicate windows.
4) Add Grafana alert: sudden >20% delta between request_count and billed_token_count for a workspace within 1 minute.
long_term_fix: Introduce a globally-consistent idempotency key for ingress attribution that is independent of tenant aliasing (compose x-rw-request-id + proxy-key-id + request-timestamp truncated to second). Update collector and usage-aggregator to dedupe by that key. Also change rebind to emit an explicit 'handoff' event so the collector can atomically mark the old handler retired before allowing writes attributed to the new handler.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement idempotency-key generation in proxy handler (backend change).
2) Update usage-collector to store and dedupe on idempotency_key (DB migration: add index on idempotency_key).
3) Add producer-side test harness simulating rebind handoffs under load.
4) Canary deploy collector changes to 5% of customers (non-enterprise) for 48 hours, monitor dedupe rate and latency impact.
5) Expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions; run a billing backfill job to correct historical duplicates for confirmed windows.
6) Post-mortem and customer communication template prepared.
acceptance_criteria: - No duplicated attribution rows for simulated rebind test in staging across 1M requests.
- Production canary shows <=0.01% duplicates in the 48h window and no latency increase >3% P95 for collector write path.
- DB migration completes in under 30 minutes and index build does not cause >5% CPU pressure on primary.
- Billing backfill tool successfully identifies and marks duplicate items for manual review.

2025-11-05 - Miguel Ortega: Able to reproduce in staging using key rebind harness. Confirmed two writes with same x-rw-request-id but different tenant_alias. Hypothesis: dedupe key isn't stable across rebinds.

2025-11-06 - Linnea Berg (billing): We found 8 invoice line-items likely impacted. Suggested short-term customer credits and flagging accounts for review. Billing team will hold charging for those windows until fix is deployed.
2025-11-08 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype changes in collector to dedupe on (request_id + proxy_key_id). Microbench showed <1% P99 latency increase. Opening PR for review.
2025-11-10 - SRE (Evan Park): Can we add an infra flag to slow rebinds for non-zero risk customers? This would reduce blast radius during rollout. Evan will coordinate with ops.
2025-11-11 - Product (Priya Sharma): Customer comms draft reviewed. Recommend offering automated credits for confirmed duplicate windows and a technical note on root cause.
2025-11-12 - Miguel Ortega: Merged collector PR to canary (5%). Monitoring alarms set. Next: DB migration PR and backfill tooling.
